error.message: No verified useful compute overlap between independent requests

iteration_notes: First 15-test integration run had two teardown errors due to a missing no-op close on InMemoryTransport; numerical and cancellation bodies passed. The corrected integration run passed all15.
A FIFO unit assertion initially observed enqueueing before the fake RPC entered; corrected to wait for the explicit queue event.
First remote run passed126 forced logit comparisons but failed the overlap gate because distinct Docker time-namespace IDs were treated as distinct clocks.

The clock-domain identity now uses kernel boot UUID plus CLOCK_MONOTONIC offset, with both Describe samples and every compute span bracketed by coordinator timestamps; malformed/unequal offsets fail validation.
The final remote run also verifies cancellation while a second request completes nine reference-matching outputs.
All final executable source hashes match the tested image; only documentation was edited after testing.
limitations: same-host correctness and overlap mechanics; no speedup claim
trusted private gRPC network without authentication or encryption
additional complete-model reference memory in validation process
uncontrolled diagnostic timings, not M5 performance results
no automatic Step retry, replay, or recovery
M4 exposes an async coordinator library and local streaming client. A standalone coordinator listener and remote benchmark adapter are M5 work.
Model thread cancellation cannot kill a running kernel; close returns false when it cannot drain. A standalone coordinator supervisor remains service-deployment work.
Overlap counts are pairs of wall-clock execution spans containing real model work, not a throughput or CPU efficiency estimate.
